title: Evidence for a sub-Jovian planet in the young TWA 7 disk
question: Can high-sensitivity thermal infrared observations with JWST/MIRI detect a sub-Jupiter mass planet responsible for the ring-like structures and gaps in the young debris disk around TWA 7?

evidence.quote: The disk around TWA 7 is one of the youngest (6.4+/- 1 Myr, [11]) debris disks known today.

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST/MIRI coronagraphic images and extract photometry and astrometry of detected sources
recipe.method: Retrieve Level 1 data from MAST, process with JWST pipeline v1.14.0, subtract background, register to coronagraph center, subtract stellar diffraction using linear combination and PCA of 9 SGD reference star frames, simulate PSF with WebbPSF and diffraction code, and extract flux/position via PSF fitting and aperture photometry.
key_parameters: Annular optimization region 0.5'' to 3'' (linear combination) and 0.5'' to 5'' with 8 PCA components; 1.5 λ/D photometric extraction area; roll 1 only used for photometry.
assumptions: Flat field correction is skipped as inappropriate for the MIRI coronagraph.

recipe.goal: Re-image archival ALMA Band 7 data and measure upper limit at CC#1 position
recipe.method: Retrieve pipeline-calibrated visibility datasets from the ALMA archive, image single epochs and combined visibilities in CASA using tclean (mosaic mode for combined) with Briggs 0.5 and natural weighting, and measure primary-beam-corrected 3-sigma upper limit at CC#1 location.
key_parameters: Hogbom deconvolution down to a residual threshold of 0.1 mJy (~3x RMS); Briggs 0.5 weighting and natural weighting.
assumptions: Evaluated upper limit assuming CC#1 is an unresolved point source that had not moved between 2016 and 2024.

recipe.goal: Fit astrometry and morphology of the bright ALMA East source and compare with MIRI East source
recipe.method: Fit a point-source model in the visibility domain to each of the 3 ALMA epochs using MCMC (emcee) to obtain astrometry, fit a 2D Gaussian to the combined image to measure integrated flux and size, and translate the ALMA position to the 2024 MIRI epoch using Gaia DR3 stellar proper motion.
key_parameters: ALMA astrometric systematic error of 5% of the beam size (9 mas for combined observation) added in quadrature to statistical MCMC uncertainties.
assumptions: The East source is extragalactic and stationary between the 2016 ALMA and 2024 MIRI epochs.

recipe.goal: Derive VLT/SPHERE near-IR upper limits at the position of CC#1
recipe.method: Reanalyse archival VLT/SPHERE IRDIS H2-H3 high-contrast imaging data from the SHINE survey using the PACO algorithm to compute 5-sigma contrast curves and flux upper limits.
key_parameters: H2 (1.593 ± 0.055 μm) and H3 (1.667 ± 0.056 μm) filters; 5-sigma confidence level.
assumptions: Local patch noise statistics modeled through mixtures of scaled multivariate Gaussians.

recipe.goal: Estimate background galaxy contamination probability and rule out solar system object
recipe.method: Check proper motion across 2-hour exposures against solar system ephemerides; combine JWST 11 μm source counts, GOODS 8 μm infrared luminosity functions at z=0.1-1, and 14 SWIRE starburst/AGN templates scaled to 22 μJy at 11 μm subject to ALMA 870 μm and SPHERE 1.6 μm upper limits.
key_parameters: 11 μm flux = 22 μJy; 870 μm upper limit = 96 μJy (or 76 μJy); 1.6 μm upper limit = 0.6 μJy (point source) to 60 μJy (extended 0.6 arcsec); redshift range z = 0.1 to 1; radius = 1.5''.
assumptions: Assumed 80% star-forming galaxies and 20% active nuclei, equal probability among star-forming templates, and up to 30% error increase for galaxy clustering.

recipe.goal: Estimate planet mass and effective temperature via atmospheric and evolutionary modeling
recipe.method: Perform MCMC forward modeling with the HADES code incorporating water clouds to fit the JWST F1140C flux and VLT/SPHERE H2/H3 5-sigma upper limits, and compare with Linder et al. [29] evolutionary cooling models.
key_parameters: System age = 6.4 +/- 1 Myr; Uniform priors: Mass [0.01, 2] M_J, Metallicity [Fe/H] [-2, 1.6], Core mass [1, 40] M_E, Effective temperature [1, 2000] K, Cloud sedimentation rate [1, 5].
assumptions: Planet and star are coeval (6.4 +/- 1 Myr); atmosphere contains water clouds.

recipe.goal: Simulate dynamical interaction between the candidate planet and the TWA 7 debris disk
recipe.method: Run symplectic N-body simulations over 6 Myr using swift_rmvs3 with a 0.34 M_J planet at 52 au on a circular orbit interacting with a flat disk of 200,000 massless planetesimals.
key_parameters: Planet mass = 0.34 M_J, semi-major axis = 52 au, circular orbit, disk inclination ~13°, 200,000 massless particles between 20 and 130 au, initial surface density ∝ r^-1, integration time = 6 Myr.
assumptions: Planet and disk are coplanar; planet orbit is circular; particles are massless planetesimals (radiation pressure on dust grains not included).

score_reason: Archival ALMA, JWST, VLT/SPHERE, and Gaia datasets are publicly identified with program IDs, and the ALMA imaging parameters (tclean, Hogbom, 0.1 mJy threshold, Briggs 0.5 and natural weighting) and MCMC astrometric procedure are well described, though custom JWST scripts and minor CASA parameters (cell size, CASA version) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA archival data (2015.1.01015.S) and JWST data (#3662) are public, the imaging and visibility-fitting recipes are straightforward, and the key quantitative results (ALMA 76 μJy upper limit, 4.0 mJy galaxy flux, astrometric offsets, and planet mass/Teff fits) are clearly specified.
